description.short_caption: Gram stain showing branching filamentous bacteria from a blood culture.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a Gram stain of a blood culture specimen. The field contains numerous branching, filamentous structures consistent with filamentous bacteria. The organisms appear Gram-positive, as indicated by their reddish-purple staining. The background is relatively clear, with no visible host cells or debris, suggesting a pure culture.
visible_findings: clear background with no visible host cells

description.short_caption: Gram stain showing gram-positive rods and cocci from a blood culture.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a Gram stain of a blood culture specimen. Numerous gram-positive rods and cocci are visible, stained pinkish-red, indicating a Gram-positive reaction. The rods appear in short chains or singly, while the cocci are clustered. The background is clear, consistent with a de-identified laboratory preparation.

This image shows a culture plate with bacterial growth on MacConkey agar, a selective and differential medium. The plate displays areas of bacterial colonies, some of which appear to have a pink hue, indicating lactose fermentation. The medium itself is a pale reddish color, characteristic of MacConkey agar. A black bar obscures identifying text on the plate.

description.short_caption: Chest radiograph showing thoracic structures and potential abnormalities.
description.detailed_description: This is a frontal chest radiograph showing the thoracic cavity. The lungs are visible bilaterally, with no overt consolidation or effusion apparent. The cardiac silhouette appears within normal limits, and the diaphragm is well-defined. The bony structures, including the ribs, clavicles, and spine, are visible. There is no clear evidence of pneumothorax or gross pathology, but further clinical correlation is recommended.

description.short_caption: Bacterial colonies on blood agar plate.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a blood agar plate with visible bacterial colonies. The colonies are distributed along streak lines, suggesting an isolation streaking technique was used. The blood agar medium appears red, indicating it is intact and not hemolyzed in most areas. Some colonies may show subtle hemolysis, but this is not prominent in the image.

description.short_caption: Chlorazol black staining of stool specimen showing Blastocystis hominis cysts.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a stool specimen stained with Chlorazol black, highlighting multiple round to oval cystic structures consistent with Blastocystis hominis. The cysts are darkly stained with a clear central area, and their size and morphology are characteristic of this organism. The background contains amorphous debris and other non-specific elements.
visible_findings: dark staining with clear central areas

Case_10007/figure6.jpg.source_caption: Chlorazol black staining of stool specimen, with Dientamoeba fragilis trophozoites.

description.short_caption: Chlorazol black staining of stool showing Dientamoeba fragilis trophozoites.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a stool specimen stained with Chlorazol black. The trophozoites of Dientamoeba fragilis are visible, appearing as rounded or slightly irregular structures with faint internal details. The background consists of other debris and cellular material, which is less prominently stained. The labeling in the image highlights the trophozoites for identification.
